metadata.note: Each test case contains realistic meeting transcripts with manually annotated expected commitments

test_cases.title: Simple explicit commitments
test_cases.transcript: Alice: I'll send the report by Friday. Bob: Great, I can review it by Saturday.

test_cases.title: Collective commitments
test_cases.transcript: Sarah: We'll launch the feature next week. Mike: Let's schedule a planning meeting for Monday.

test_cases.title: Named person in collective
test_cases.transcript: Priya: Let's have Vikram run the performance tests by Wednesday.

test_cases.title: Dependency-based commitment
test_cases.transcript: Rahul: Once the database migration is complete, I'll update the API by October 12th.

test_cases.title: Multiple dates in one commitment
test_cases.transcript: David: I need the requirements by Friday and the prototype by the following Monday.

test_cases.title: Explicit calendar date
test_cases.transcript: Emma: We'll finalize the budget on October 15th. Jack: I'll send the invoice by October 20th.

test_cases.title: Non-commitments (should extract 0)
test_cases.transcript: Alice: What do you think about the new design? Bob: It looks good. Charlie: Let's discuss it more in the next meeting.

test_cases.title: Mixed: commitment and non-commitment
test_cases.transcript: Maria: Do you think we should update the docs? Leo: I can update them by end of week. Anna: Let's check with the team first.

test_cases.title: Tentative commitment (low confidence)
test_cases.transcript: Chris: I could try to optimize the performance if I get some time.

test_cases.title: Request vs commitment
test_cases.transcript: Manager: Can someone review the code? Engineer: Sure, I'll review it today.

test_cases.title: Relative dates
test_cases.transcript: Sam: I'll finalize the proposal in 3 days. Taylor: I can review tomorrow.

test_cases.title: Multi-person meeting with multiple commitments
test_cases.transcript: Priya: Alright everyone, let's plan the Q4 launch. Vikram: I can have the database ready by October 8th. Rahul: Once that's done, I'll complete the API by October 11th. Ananya: I'll update the UI by October 10th.

test_cases.title: Past tense (no commitment)
test_cases.transcript: Lisa: I sent the files yesterday. Mark: Great, I already reviewed them.

test_cases.title: Hedged language
test_cases.transcript: Alex: We might need to update the deployment script. Jordan: We should probably test it more thoroughly.

test_cases.title: Complex commitment with condition
test_cases.transcript: Casey: If we get approval, I'll start the implementation by October 5th. Otherwise, we'll wait until next month.

test_cases.title: Real-world: Mixed agenda meeting
test_cases.transcript: Emily: Thanks everyone for joining. Let's review our status. Thomas: I finished the documentation like I said. Emily: Great! Now, can someone ensure the tests pass? Patricia: I can run the full test suite tomorrow and send you the report. Michael: Should we also verify the API responses? Emily: Yes, let's do that. Michael, can you handle it? Michael: Sure, I'll validate all the endpoints by Friday. Diana: I'll update the wiki with the new process by end of week.

expected_commitments.description: Run the full test suite and send report
Update the wiki with the new process

test_cases.title: Continuity example: Commitment mentioned in follow-up
test_cases.transcript: Meeting 1 - Sarah: I'll have the proposal ready by next Friday. Meeting 2 (one week later) - Sarah: The proposal is done as I promised.
test_cases.note: This represents a commitment from Meeting 1 that should be linked to Meeting 2 via Commitment Continuity

metrics.true_positives: Commitments correctly extracted with owner, description, and date
metrics.false_positives: Items extracted that are not commitments (requests, questions, discussions)
metrics.false_negatives: Commitments in transcript that were not extracted
metrics.precision: TP / (TP + FP) - What fraction of extractions were correct
metrics.recall: TP / (TP + FN) - What fraction of actual commitments were found

per_test_evaluation.owner_match: Does extracted owner match expected owner (case-insensitive)?
per_test_evaluation.description_match: Is the action description semantically correct?
per_test_evaluation.date_match: Is the due date (or phrase) captured correctly?

target_performance.notes: These targets are realistic for LLM-based extraction with diverse language patterns
